## figma
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

FILE SESSION:
Once the target fileKey is known, call create_session with that key and a concise task description before search_design_system, get_libraries, use_figma, or any other file tool. This applies to read-only tasks too. If a new file is needed, call create_new_file first, then create_session with the returned file key. Reuse the returned UUID as the sessionId argument on eligible file tools for subsequent work on that task, including calls to other files.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

SKILLS (Prefer the skills shipped with the Figma plugin on the agent being used. If no Figma plugin is installed, use the skills served by the Figma MCP resource):
- /figma-use — MANDATORY before calling use_figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-design — for translating an app page or layout into Figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-design/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-library — for building a design system in Figma from code; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-library/SKILL.md
- /figma-code-connect — for mapping Figma components to codebase components; fallback: skill://figma/figma-code-connect/SKILL.md
- /figma-use-figjam — for FigJam-specific use_figma flows; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use-figjam/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-diagram — MANDATORY before calling generate_diagram; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-diagram/SKILL.md
- /figma-design-to-code — MANDATORY before calling get_design_context; fallback: skill://figma/figma-design-to-code/SKILL.md

URL PARSING:
Extract fileKey and nodeId from Figma URLs:
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → convert "-" to ":" in nodeId
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName → use branchKey as fileKey
- figma.com/make/:makeFileKey/:makeFileName → use makeFileKey
- figma.com/board/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → FigJam file, use get_figjam
- figma.com/slides/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → Figma Slides file
- figma.com/spec/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → Figma Specs file, load the figma-spec skill and use use_figma

DESIGN-TO-CODE WORKFLOW (Figma → code):
MANDATORY: load the /figma-design-to-code skill BEFORE calling get_design_context — it carries the full workflow (adapting the reference, reusing existing project components and tokens, and honoring the response's hints by priority). content.content:
1	---
     2	name: jusprin-release
     3	description: Use when asked to make, prepare or start a new JusPrin release (a new version on GitHub), from choosing the commit range to the after-publish steps. Covers the version, release notes, server readiness, translations, the error-handling audit, tests, the guide check, moving main, the release workflow, testing the draft and what follows publishing. Not for JusPrin 1 (jusprin-v1) or OrcaSlicer's own releases.
     4	---
     5	
     6	# Making a JusPrin release
     7	
     8	The release workflow, `.github/workflows/jusprin_release.yml`, builds the
     9	release files from one commit and uploads them to a draft release on GitHub.
    10	It refuses the commit without a new version, release notes, a guide check and
    11	the Sentry secrets, and fails a platform whose debug files or page source
    12	maps did not reach Sentry (see "Releasing" in `AGENTS.md`). It does not run the test suites, check the
    13	server, check the translations or audit error handling. This skill covers
    14	those too, in the order they have to happen.
    15	
    16	## Kenneth decides these
    17	
    18	Ask Kenneth, in plain words, and wait for his yes before each of these. A yes
    19	covers that one action, not the next one.
    20	
    21	- The version number, when he has not named it.
    22	- The release notes' wording. Show him the file.
    23	- Deploying the server.
    24	- Which error-handling findings must be fixed before the release.
    25	- Taking in commits that landed on `jusprin-dev` after the range was fixed.
    26	- The Sentry values and read-only token for checking the draft.
    27	- Spending API money on live AI checks. Say the cost.
    28	- Pushing to `jusprin-dev`, and moving `main` forward.
    29	- Starting the release workflow.
    30	- Downloading the draft's files to this computer.
    31	- Posting anything on GitHub, such as replies to issues.
    32	
    33	**Never publish the draft.** Kenneth publishes it by hand on the Releases page.
    34	Never force-push `main`.
    35	
    36	## 1. Set up
    37	
    38	1. Check that the main checkout (the folder that holds `jusprin-dev`, not a
    39	   worktree) has nothing that would be left out of the release:
    40	
    41	   ```bash
    42	   git -C <main checkout> fetch origin
    43	   git -C <main checkout> status --porcelain -uno
    44	   git -C <main checkout> log --oneline origin/jusprin-dev..jusprin-dev
    45	   ```
    46	
    47	   Both must print nothing. A changed file or a commit that is not on GitHub
    48	   is work someone may expect in the release. Stop, list each one for
    49	   Kenneth, and wait until he has pushed it or said to leave it out. Do not
    50	   push, commit or discard it yourself. Untracked files do not block: they
    51	   are working docs Kenneth keeps there on purpose.
    52	2. Find the last release: `git tag --list 'jusprin/v*' --sort=-v:refname | head -1`.
    53	   Write down the commit `origin/jusprin-dev` points to now
    54	   (`git rev-parse origin/jusprin-dev`). The range is the last release's tag
    55	   to that commit, and every later step checks that range. Step 8 checks
    56	   whether `jusprin-dev` moved since.
    57	3. Make your own worktree at that commit, under `<repo>/.claude/worktrees/`,
    58	   on a branch named `claude/release-<version>`. Never name it
    59	   `jusprin-release/...`: pushing a branch with that name starts an unsigned
    60	   release build. If that branch name is taken, add a suffix.
    61	4. Read every commit in the range: `git log --format='%h %s%n%b' <range>`.
    62	   Note what a person would notice, and the GitHub issues each change fixes.
    63	
    64	## 2. Version and release notes
    65	
    66	1. Set `kVersion` in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp`. It must be
    67	   above every released JusPrin version.
    68	2. Write `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release-notes/<version>.md`. The app
    69	   shows this file under "What's new", and the draft starts with it. Follow the
    70	   shape of the previous release's file. Write for a person who prints, not for
    71	   a developer. Check every on-screen label you quote against the source
    72	   (`git grep`), and leave out anything you have not checked.
    73	3. A change that sends anything new from the person's computer, such as a new
    74	   message to our server, goes in the notes and says what it holds.
    75	
    76	## 3. Server readiness
    77	
    78	The app calls JusPrin's server at `https://jusprinv2.obico.io`. Every address
    79	the release calls must already be deployed there.
    80	
    81	Many addresses are joined from pieces, so no single search finds them all.
    82	List them from the code that builds them:
    83	
    84	```bash
    85	git grep -n -E '"/(ent|o|accounts|jusprin)/|"/models"|ask_server\("' -- src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin ':!*test*'
    86	```
    87	
    88	Read each hit and write out the full path. For example, `ask_server("code/confirm", …)`
    89	in `Agent/CloudAccount.cpp` is `/ent/jusprin/v2/auth/code/confirm`, and the
    90	model list is the gateway's address with its last part replaced by `/models`.
    91	Leave off any query string. Check full paths only, never a bare prefix such
    92	as `/ent/jusprin/v2/auth/`.
    93	
    94	GET each one: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://jusprinv2.obico.io<path>`.
    95	Any answer but 404 (200, 400, 401, 403, 405) means the address is there. A 404
    96	means it is not deployed. Find the server change in the tsd-enterprise
    97	repository (`web_ent/jusprin/v2/urls.py` on `master`), tell Kenneth what is
    98	missing, and wait until it is deployed. Also tell him about any other server
    99	behavior a change in the range relies on, such as a new error code.
   100	
   101	## 4. Translations
   102	
   103	1. Run `python3 src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/update_catalogs.py`. It
   104	   needs GNU gettext and `npm ci` in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI`. If it
   105	   changes any catalog, those changes go into the release commit.
   106	2. Translate every new entry in every language, as
   107	   `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/README.md` says. Those catalogs are
   108	   JusPrin's own, in `Localization/native/` and `Localization/pages/`. Never
   109	   edit upstream's `localization/i18n/` and never run `run_gettext`. From
   110	   "Localization & translations" in `AGENTS.md` and the `orca-translations`
   111	   skill, take only the editing rules and the glossary.
   112	3. `npx vitest run src/catalogs.test.ts` in `AgentUI` must pass: it fails
   113	   while an entry is untranslated or a translation lost a placeholder.
   114	4. Count the entries marked `# Needs human review` in
   115	   `Localization/native/*.po` and `Localization/pages/*.po`. Tell Kenneth the
   116	   count, so he can decide whether someone should read a language.
   117	
   118	These steps cannot find a sentence nobody marked for translation. While
   119	reading the range, look for text a person reads that is not marked.
   120	
   121	## 5. Error-handling audit
   122	
   123	Run the `error-handling` skill on the range. When the release relies on
   124	server changes, also audit the tsd-enterprise commits under `web_ent/jusprin/`
   125	on `master` since the previous release tag's date (that repository has no
   126	release tags).
   127	
   128	Report the findings to Kenneth and wait. He says which ones must be fixed
   129	before the release. A fix is its own commit on `jusprin-dev`, and pushing it
   130	needs his yes like any push. Once it is pushed, restart from step 1 with the
   131	new range.
   132	
   133	## 6. Tests
   134	
   135	Build in your worktree, in Release, following "Building on a shared machine"
   136	in `AGENTS.md`: check the load first, use `-j4`, choose every target before
   137	you start. A new worktree has no dependencies of its own, so configure it
   138	against the main checkout's, with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake`
   139	(Homebrew's cmake fails to find Eigen3):
   140	
   141	```bash
   142	cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
   143	  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
   144	  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=<main checkout>/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local \
   145	  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
   146	  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
   147	```
   148	
   149	Node must be on `PATH` for the pages. Pass build directories as absolute
   150	paths: the shell's folder can change between commands.
   151	
   152	- macOS: build `agent_bridge_tests`, `jusprin_tests`, `shell_integration_harness`,
   153	  `tool_call_check`, `jusprin_web` and `jusprin_catalogs` in one build, then
   154	  run both test programs and `npm test` in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI`
   155	  and `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/HomeUI`.
   156	- Windows and Linux: the release workflow neither builds nor runs the tests,
   157	  so nothing else shows they even compile there. Build them and run
   158	  `agent_bridge_tests` and `jusprin_tests` on each, with `build_win.bat -s --tests`
   159	  on Windows and `./build_linux.sh -st` on Linux. Kenneth keeps test machines
   160	  for both. Ask him for access if you do not have it, and say in your report
   161	  if they were not run.
   162	- When the range changes text the model reads (prompts, skills, tool
   163	  descriptions, tool results, how history is sent), run the live prompt suite
   164	  (`tests/project_prompt/README.md`, and `tests/printer_prompt` when printer
   165	  chats changed). Its `claude-cli` backend costs no API money. The README
   166	  also asks for a small paid run on the app's default model before a release.
   167	  Propose it to Kenneth with its cost, and run it only after his yes.
   168	
   169	Report each failure with its output. A failure in the range is a bug to fix
   170	on `jusprin-dev` before the release, not a reason to skip the step.
   171	
   172	## 7. Guide check
   173	
   174	Follow "Before a release" in `docs/guide/README.md`, on the build from step 6
   175	with the new version already in `Version.hpp`.
   176	
   177	1. Tell Kenneth first: the command drives the app on this computer's screen
   178	   for about a minute a page, so nobody should use the computer meanwhile.
   179	2. Look through `git log <range> -- src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin` for new screens or
   180	   menu items no page mentions, and add them to the guide. Do this first: the
   181	   check below cannot find them, and a page changed after it passes was not
   182	   checked.
   183	3. Run `scripts/check_guide.py --ask-ai` and fix what it reports until it
   184	   passes. It then writes the version to `docs/guide/checked-version.txt`. If
   185	   you change any page afterwards, run it again.
   186	
   187	## 8. Commit and land
   188	
   189	1. Commit the version, the notes, the catalogs and the guide files on your
   190	   branch. Make sure no temporary working docs or screenshots are in it.
   191	2. Run `git fetch origin` and compare `origin/jusprin-dev` with the commit you
   192	   wrote down in step 1. If it moved, those new commits have had none of the
   193	   checks above. List them for Kenneth, rebase onto `origin/jusprin-dev`, and
   194	   repeat steps 3 to 7 for them before landing.
   195	3. With Kenneth's yes, land it on `jusprin-dev` without a merge commit:
   196	   `git push origin HEAD:jusprin-dev`. Then bring the main checkout along:
   197	   `git -C <main checkout> pull --ff-only`. Write down your commit
   198	   (`git rev-parse HEAD`). This is the release commit.
   199	4. With Kenneth's yes, move `main` to that exact commit:
   200	   `git push origin <release commit>:main`. This only succeeds as a fast
   201	   forward. If it is refused, stop and tell Kenneth. Never force it.
   202	
   203	## 9. Start the release workflow
   204	
   205	Only the release publisher may run it: the repository variable
   206	`JUSPRIN_RELEASE_PUBLISHER`, or `kennethjiang` when that is unset. Check that
   207	`gh api user -q .login` prints that name.
   208	
   209	The workflow refuses to start without five Sentry secrets:
   210	`JUSPRIN_SENTRY_DSN` (the project the app sends reports to), and
   211	`SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN`, `SENTRY_URL`, `SENTRY_ORG` and `SENTRY_PROJECT` (which
   212	upload the debug files and page source maps that let Sentry name the
   213	functions in a stack, with file and line). The `gh` token on this computer
   214	cannot list secrets (`gh secret list` answers 403), so do not try. If the
   215	run's first job fails on a missing secret, tell Kenneth which one. Only he
   216	can add it.
   217	
   218	With his yes:
   219	
   220	```bash
   221	gh workflow run jusprin_release.yml --ref main -f sign_macos=true
   222	gh run list --workflow jusprin_release.yml --limit 1 --json databaseId,headSha
   223	```
   224	
   225	Check that the run's `headSha` is the release commit. Keep Mac signing on:
   226	Homebrew refuses a Mac app that is not signed and notarised. Wait for the run
   227	in the background (`gh run watch <databaseId>`). If its "Upload to the draft
   228	release" job waits for an approval (the `release` environment can require
   229	one), tell Kenneth. A failed run is a failure to report with its log, not a
   230	reason to tick a skip box.
   231	
   232	## 10. Test the draft
   233	
   234	The draft holds the Windows installer and portable zip, the Mac disk image,
   235	the Linux AppImage and `SHA256SUMS.txt`. These files are what people will get,
   236	so test them, not a local build. Ask Kenneth before downloading them.
   237	
   238	On each platform: install over the previous release and start the app. Check
   239	that Preferences shows the new version, sign in, have one chat, slice, and
   240	check each fix in the notes on the platform where it mattered (for example a
   241	locale bug on Windows, where it always shows).
   242	
   243	Check that Sentry can read this release's stacks, on the draft's own files.
   244	Both scripts read `SENTRY_URL`, `SENTRY_ORG`, `SENTRY_PROJECT` and
   245	`SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` from the environment. GitHub secrets cannot be read back,
   246	so ask Kenneth for the values and for a token that can only read the
   247	project. Set them in the shell for these commands only, and never write
   248	them into a file.
   249	
   250	- Run `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/sentry_debug_files.sh verify <file>`
   251	  on the Mac app's `Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer` (it checks both
   252	  architectures), Windows' `OrcaSlicer.dll` and the AppImage's
   253	  `bin/orca-slicer` (`--appimage-extract` puts it under `squashfs-root`).
   254	  Each must print "Sentry holds debug information".
   255	- Run `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/sentry_page_maps.sh verify <folder>`
   256	  from the release commit, with the folder that holds `jusprin/agent` and
   257	  `jusprin/home` in each platform's app: the Mac app's `Contents/Resources`,
   258	  the Windows install's `resources`, the AppImage's `squashfs-root/resources`.
   259	  Each must print "Sentry holds the agent page's source map" and the same
   260	  for home.
   261	- Send one error report from the installed app and open it in Sentry
   262	  (the project `SENTRY_PROJECT` names, filter
   263	  `release:"<the app line it shows>"`): the
   264	  frames of the app's own code must show function names with file and line,
   265	  not only addresses.
   266	
   267	Before Kenneth publishes, check `gh workflow list --all | grep -i winget`.
   268	`winget_updater.yml` is inherited from OrcaSlicer. It runs when a release is
   269	published and submits the installer to winget as `SoftFever.OrcaSlicer`. It
   270	must say `disabled_manually`. If it is enabled, tell Kenneth before he
   271	publishes.
   272	
   273	Tell Kenneth what was tested on which platform and what was not. He publishes.
   274	
   275	## 11. After publishing
   276	
   277	- Start the previous release on one computer and check that Preferences ›
   278	  Updates offers the new version. The update check reads only published
   279	  releases, so this is the first moment it can be checked.
   280	- Reply to and close the GitHub issues the release fixes, with Kenneth's yes.
   281	- Update JusPrin's Homebrew cask to the new version, if the cask is in
   282	  Homebrew.
   283	- Open the newest events in Sentry for the new release and check that a
   284	  report's or crash's stack names the app's functions with file and line,
   285	  and that a page error's frames name the page's source files
   286	  (`HomeUI/src/...`, `AgentUI/src/...`). A stack of bare addresses or of
   287	  `app:///home/index.html` positions means a platform's debug files or a
   288	  page's map are missing: run `sentry_debug_files.sh verify` or
   289	  `sentry_page_maps.sh verify` on that platform's released files.
   290	- The next day, run the `jusprin-production-check` skill in the tsd-enterprise
   291	  repository for new failures from the new version.
   292	- Remove your worktree and branch.
SKILL.md

# MCP Server Instructions

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## figma
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

FILE SESSION:
Once the target fileKey is known, call create_session with that key and a concise task description before search_design_system, get_libraries, use_figma, or any other file tool. This applies to read-only tasks too. If a new file is needed, call create_new_file first, then create_session with the returned file key. Reuse the returned UUID as the sessionId argument on eligible file tools for subsequent work on that task, including calls to other files.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

SKILLS (Prefer the skills shipped with the Figma plugin on the agent being used. If no Figma plugin is installed, use the skills served by the Figma MCP resource):
- /figma-use — MANDATORY before calling use_figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-design — for translating an app page or layout into Figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-design/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-library — for building a design system in Figma from code; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-library/SKILL.md
- /figma-code-connect — for mapping Figma components to codebase components; fallback: skill://figma/figma-code-connect/SKILL.md
- /figma-use-figjam — for FigJam-specific use_figma flows; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use-figjam/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-diagram — MANDATORY before calling generate_diagram; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-diagram/SKILL.md
- /figma-design-to-code — MANDATORY before calling get_design_context; fallback: skill://figma/figma-design-to-code/SKILL.md

URL PARSING:
Extract fileKey and nodeId from Figma URLs:
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → convert "-" to ":" in nodeId
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName → use branchKey as fileKey
- figma.com/make/:makeFileKey/:makeFileName → use makeFileKey
- figma.com/board/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → FigJam file, use get_figjam
- figma.com/slides/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → Figma Slides file
- figma.com/spec/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → Figma Specs file, load the figma-spec skill and use use_figma

DESIGN-TO-CODE WORKFLOW (Figma → code):
MANDATORY: load the /figma-design-to-code skill BEFORE calling get_design_context — it carries the full workflow (adapting the reference, reusing existing project components and tokens, and honoring the response's hints by priority). CODE-TO-DESIGN WORKFLOW (code → Figma):

     1	name: JusPrin release
     2	
     3	# Builds JusPrin from one commit and uploads the files to a DRAFT GitHub
     4	# release. It never publishes anything.
     5	#
     6	# - The version is the one in src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp, and
     7	#   the draft is tagged jusprin/v<version>, as JusPrin 1.4.0 was (the repo
     8	#   still holds OrcaSlicer's own v2.x tags). GitHub creates that tag only when
     9	#   the draft is published, by hand, on the Releases page. JusPrin's update
    10	#   check reads the public release list, which never includes drafts, so
    11	#   users see nothing until then.
    12	# - It stops if that version is already released, is not above every
    13	#   released JusPrin version, or its tag already exists
    14	#   (Packaging/release.mjs), and if
    15	#   Packaging/release-notes/<version>.md, the notes the draft starts with and
    16	#   that the app shows under "What's new", is missing.
    17	# - It stops if a Sentry secret is missing (JUSPRIN_SENTRY_DSN, the project
    18	#   the app reports to; SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN, SENTRY_URL, SENTRY_ORG and
    19	#   SENTRY_PROJECT, which upload the debug files and source maps), and each
    20	#   platform's build fails unless Sentry then holds the app's own code's
    21	#   debug information, with file and line (Packaging/sentry_debug_files.sh),
    22	#   and each page's source map (Packaging/sentry_page_maps.sh).
    23	# - It also stops if the guide was not checked for this version
    24	#   (docs/guide/checked-version.txt, written by scripts/check_guide.py
    25	#   --ask-ai; see docs/guide/README.md), unless "Release without the guide
    26	#   check" is ticked. Then the draft's title says the guide was not checked.
    27	# - Running it again for the same version replaces the draft's files.
    28	# - Files: Windows x64 installer and portable zip, macOS universal disk image,
    29	#   Linux x64 AppImage, and SHA256SUMS.txt.
    30	# - Only the release publisher can run it: the repo variable
    31	#   JUSPRIN_RELEASE_PUBLISHER, or kennethjiang when it is unset.
    32	# - Signing: macOS when "sign_macos" is ticked, with the Apple secrets JusPrin
    33	#   1.x used. The box starts ticked: Homebrew's cask rules reject a Mac app
    34	#   that is not signed and notarised. A release started by pushing a branch
    35	#   is never signed. Windows builds are unsigned. An unsigned draft says so
    36	#   in its title.
    37	#
    38	# Start it from Actions > JusPrin release > Run workflow (the file must also
    39	# be on the default branch for that button), or by pushing a branch named
    40	# jusprin-release/<anything>.
    41	
    42	on:
    43	  workflow_dispatch:
    44	    inputs:
    45	      sign_macos:
    46	        description: 'Sign and notarise the macOS app with the Apple secrets'
    47	        type: boolean
    48	        default: true
    49	      skip_guide_check:
    50	        description: 'Release without the guide check'
    51	        type: boolean
    52	        default: false
    53	  push:
    54	    branches:
    55	      - 'jusprin-release/**'
    56	
    57	permissions:
    58	  contents: write   # create the draft and upload its files
    59	  actions: read
    60	
    61	concurrency:
    62	  group: jusprin-release
    63	  cancel-in-progress: false
    64	
    65	jobs:
    66	  prepare:
    67	    name: Check the version
    68	    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    69	    outputs:
    70	      version: ${{ steps.check.outputs.version }}
    71	      tag: ${{ steps.check.outputs.tag }}
    72	      prerelease: ${{ steps.check.outputs.prerelease }}
    73	      draft_id: ${{ steps.check.outputs.draft_id }}
    74	      guide_checked: ${{ steps.guide.outputs.checked }}
    75	    steps:
    76	      - name: Only the release publisher
    77	        env:
    78	          PUBLISHER: ${{ vars.JUSPRIN_RELEASE_PUBLISHER || 'kennethjiang' }}
    79	        run: |
    80	          if [ "$GITHUB_ACTOR" != "$PUBLISHER" ]; then
    81	            echo "::error::Only @$PUBLISHER may make a JusPrin release (this run is @$GITHUB_ACTOR's)."
    82	            exit 1
    83	          fi
    84	
    85	      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
    86	        with:
    87	          sparse-checkout: |
    88	            src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin
    89	            docs/guide
    90	
    91	      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
    92	        with:
    93	          node-version: '24'
    94	
    95	      - name: Test the release checks
    96	        run: node --test src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release.test.mjs
    97	
    98	      - name: Check the version against the releases
    99	        id: check
   100	        env:
   101	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
   102	        run: |
   103	          gh api --paginate --slurp "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/releases?per_page=100" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/releases.json"
   104	          gh api --paginate "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/matching-refs/tags/" --jq '.[].ref' > "$RUNNER_TEMP/tags.txt"
   105	          node src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release.mjs check src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp \
   106	            "$RUNNER_TEMP/releases.json" "$RUNNER_TEMP/tags.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
   107	
   108	      - name: Require the release notes
   109	        run: |
   110	          notes="src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release-notes/${{ steps.check.outputs.version }}.md"
   111	          if [ ! -s "$notes" ]; then
   112	            echo "::error::Write $notes first. The draft starts with it and the app shows it under What's new."
   113	            exit 1
   114	          fi
   115	          if grep -q '^PLACEHOLDER' "$notes"; then
   116	            echo "::warning::$notes is still the placeholder. Replace it before publishing the draft."
   117	          fi
   118	
   119	      - name: Require the Sentry secrets
   120	        env:

1	name: JusPrin release build
     2	
     3	# One platform of a JusPrin release, called by jusprin_release.yml.
     4	#
     5	# The build is OrcaSlicer's: its dependency workflow (build_deps.yml), cached
     6	# under the key OrcaSlicer's build_check_cache.yml uses, and its build
     7	# scripts. Only the packaging is JusPrin's (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging).
     8	# OrcaSlicer's build_orca.yml can't be reused as it is: its Linux step looks
     9	# for OrcaSlicer_Linux_V<version>.AppImage, which a JusPrin build never
    10	# writes, and its packaging steps name everything OrcaSlicer.
    11	
    12	on:
    13	  workflow_call:
    14	    inputs:
    15	      os:
    16	        required: true
    17	        type: string
    18	      # x64 (Windows), arm64 or x86_64 (macOS); empty for Linux amd64, as in
    19	      # OrcaSlicer's build_all.yml.
    20	      arch:
    21	        required: false
    22	        type: string
    23	        default: ''
    24	      version:
    25	        required: true
    26	        type: string
    27	
    28	jobs:
    29	  cache:
    30	    name: Find the deps cache
    31	    # GitHub often has no hosted macOS runner free, and cancels a job that gets
    32	    # none within 15 minutes, so the macOS lookup runs on Linux, as in
    33	    # OrcaSlicer's build_check_cache.yml.
    34	    runs-on: ${{ startsWith(inputs.os, 'macos-') && 'ubuntu-24.04' || inputs.os }}
    35	    outputs:
    36	      key: ${{ steps.key.outputs.key }}
    37	      path: ${{ steps.key.outputs.path }}
    38	      hit: ${{ steps.lookup.outputs.cache-hit }}
    39	    steps:
    40	      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
    41	        with:
    42	          lfs: 'false'
    43	      - name: Compute the key
    44	        id: key
    45	        shell: bash
    46	        env:
    47	          # As in OrcaSlicer's build_check_cache.yml. The macOS and Linux trees are
    48	          # OrcaSlicer's and share its cache; OrcaSlicer builds Windows with clang-cl,
    49	          # so JusPrin's cl tree is cached on its own.
    50	          cache_os: ${{ startsWith(inputs.os, 'macos-') && format('{0}-{1}', inputs.os, inputs.arch) || (runner.os == 'Windows' && format('windows-{0}-msvc', inputs.arch) || format('linux-clang{0}', inputs.arch && format('-{0}', inputs.arch) || '')) }}
    51	          OS: ${{ inputs.os }}
    52	          dep_folder: ${{ startsWith(inputs.os, 'macos-') && format('/{0}', inputs.arch) || (runner.os == 'Windows' && inputs.arch == 'arm64') && '-arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep' || '/OrcaSlicer_dep' }}
    53	        run: |
    54	          echo "key=${cache_os}-cache-orcaslicer_deps-build-${{ hashFiles('deps/**') }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    55	          # Relative to the workspace, as build_deps.yml takes it.
    56	          echo "path=deps/build${dep_folder}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    57	          # The workspace of a hosted macOS job, where build_deps.yml saved the tree.
    58	          if [[ "$OS" == macos-* ]]; then
    59	            echo "macos_workspace=/Users/runner/work/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY#*/}/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY#*/}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    60	          fi
    61	      # actions/cache matches the path too, so a Linux lookup for macOS names the
    62	      # macOS workspace.
    63	      - name: Look the cache up
    64	        id: lookup
    65	        uses: actions/cache@v5
    66	        with:
    67	          path: ${{ steps.key.outputs.macos_workspace || github.workspace }}/${{ steps.key.outputs.path }}
    68	          key: ${{ steps.key.outputs.key }}
    69	          lookup-only: true
    70	
    71	  deps:
    72	    name: Build deps
    73	    needs: cache
    74	    if: ${{ needs.cache.outputs.hit != 'true' }}
    75	    uses: ./.github/workflows/build_deps.yml
    76	    with:
    77	      cache-key: ${{ needs.cache.outputs.key }}
    78	      cache-path: ${{ needs.cache.outputs.path }}
    79	      valid-cache: false
    80	      os: ${{ inputs.os }}
    81	      arch: ${{ inputs.arch }}
    82	      # cl under the Visual Studio generator, which JusPrin's Windows build uses.
    83	      compiler: msvc
    84	      # Stops build_deps.yml before it calls OrcaSlicer's build_orca.yml.
    85	      build-deps-only: true
    86	    secrets: inherit
    87	
    88	  build:
    89	    name: Build JusPrin
    90	    needs: [cache, deps]
    91	    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.cache.result == 'success' && (needs.deps.result == 'success' || needs.deps.result == 'skipped') }}
    92	    runs-on: ${{ inputs.os }}
    93	    env:
    94	      VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
    95	      # The Sentry project the app's error reports go to, read by
    96	      # JusPrin/sources.cmake; kept out of the public repository.
    97	      JUSPRIN_SENTRY_DSN: ${{ secrets.JUSPRIN_SENTRY_DSN }}
    98	      # The pages' build, which their error reports carry and their source
    99	      # maps are filed under in Sentry (WebShared/errorReports.ts).
   100	      JUSPRIN_PAGE_BUILD: ${{ github.sha }}
   101	    steps:
   102	      # A build without it sends no error report or crash, which nobody would
   103	      # notice until reports were needed.
   104	      - name: Require the Sentry key
   105	        shell: bash
   106	        run: |
   107	          if [ -z "$JUSPRIN_SENTRY_DSN" ]; then
   108	            echo "::error::The secret JUSPRIN_SENTRY_DSN is missing, so this build would send no error report or crash."
   109	            exit 1
   110	          fi
   111	
   112	      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
   113	        with:
   114	          lfs: 'false'
   115	
   116	      - name: Load the deps
   117	        uses: actions/cache@v5
   118	        with:
   119	          path: ${{ github.workspace }}/${{ needs.cache.outputs.path }}
   120	          key: ${{ needs.cache.outputs.key }}
   121	          fail-on-cache-miss: true
   122	
   123	      # The same CMake as OrcaSlicer's build_orca.yml.
   124	      - uses: lukka/get-cmake@latest
   125	        with:
   126	          cmakeVersion: "~4.3.0"
   127	          useLocalCache: true
   128	          useCloudCache: true
   129	
   130	      # The Agent and Home pages are built with npm (JusPrin/Web/CMakeLists.txt).
   131	      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
   132	        with:
   133	          node-version: '24'
   134	
   135	      # Windows
   136	      - name: Set up MSVC
   137	        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
   138	        uses: microsoft/setup-msbuild@v3
   139	
   140	      - name: Install NSIS
   141	        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
   142	        run: choco install nsis
   143	
   144	      - name: Build
   145	        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
   146	        shell: pwsh
   147	        # As OrcaSlicer's build_orca.yml calls build_win.bat, but with cl rather than
   148	        # clang-cl. -i installs into build\OrcaSlicer, which the packaging reads.
   149	        run: |
   150	          $deps = (Split-Path "${{ github.workspace }}/${{ needs.cache.outputs.path }}").Replace('\', '/')
   151	          .\build_win.bat -s -i --arch ${{ inputs.arch }} --build-dir build --deps-dir $deps --msvc --msbuild
   152	
   153	      - name: Package
   154	        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
   155	        shell: pwsh
   156	        run: |
   157	          ./src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/windows_package.ps1 -BuildDir build -Version $env:VERSION `
   158	            -Arch "${{ inputs.arch }}" -OutDir dist
   159	
   160	      # macOS: each architecture is built here; jusprin_release.yml joins them
   161	      # into the universal app and the disk image.
   162	      - name: Prepare the Mac
   163	        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
   164	        run: |
   165	          brew install libtool
   166	          mkdir -p "${{ github.workspace }}/deps/build/${{ inputs.arch }}"
   167	          # As OrcaSlicer's build_orca.yml does, for disk space: keep only the
   168	          # selected Xcode.
   169	          xcode=$(basename "$(cd "$(xcode-select -p)/../.." && pwd -P)")
   170	          sudo find /Applications -maxdepth 1 -type d -name "Xcode_*.app" ! -name "$xcode" -exec rm -rf {} +
   171	          sudo rm -rf ~/Library/Developer/CoreSimulator/Caches/*
   172	
   173	      - name: Build
   174	        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
   175	        # Line tables (-gline-tables-only) let Sentry give the file and line
   176	        # of each frame; they go into the dSYM below, not into the app.
   177	        run: >-
   178	          ./build_release_macos.sh -s -n -x -j 3 -a ${{ inputs.arch }} -t 10.15 --
   179	          -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS=-gline-tables-only -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS=-gline-tables-only
   180	
   181	      # The line tables stay in the build's object files; dsymutil gathers
   182	      # them into a dSYM for Sentry, and strip -S then drops the executable's
   183	      # pointers to those files. The executable keeps its function names.
   184	      - name: Split the debug information
   185	        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
   186	        run: |
   187	          bin="build/${{ inputs.arch }}/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer"
   188	          dsymutil "$bin" -o "build/${{ inputs.arch }}/OrcaSlicer.dSYM"
   189	          strip -S "$bin"
   190	
   191	      - name: Package
   192	        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
   193	        run: |
   194	          mkdir -p dist
   195	          tar -czf "dist/JusPrin_Mac_bundle_${{ inputs.arch }}.tar.gz" -C "build/${{ inputs.arch }}" OrcaSlicer
   196	
   197	      # Linux
   198	      - name: Install the build packages
   199	        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
   200	        uses: ./.github/actions/apt-install-deps
   201	
   202	      - name: Build
   203	        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
   204	        run: |
   205	          # -s builds the slicer and lays out build/package; JusPrin's AppImage
   206	          # replaces OrcaSlicer's (-i). Line tables (-gline-tables-only) let
   207	          # Sentry give the file and line of each frame; they are split off
   208	          # below, not shipped.
   209	          ./build_linux.sh -srlL -- -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS=-gline-tables-only -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS=-gline-tables-only
   210	          ./scripts/check_appimage_libs.sh ./build/package ./build/package/bin/orca-slicer
   211	
   212	      # Sentry files a debug file by the executable's GNU build id, which the
   213	      # split file keeps; without one the two would not match.
   214	      - name: Split the debug information
   215	        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
   216	        run: |
   217	          bin=build/package/bin/orca-slicer
   218	          readelf -n "$bin" | grep -q 'Build ID' || {
   219	            echo "::error::$bin has no GNU build id, so Sentry could not match its debug file to it."
   220	            exit 1
   221	          }
   222	          objcopy --only-keep-debug "$bin" build/orca-slicer.debug
   223	          objcopy --strip-debug --add-gnu-debuglink=build/orca-slicer.debug "$bin"
   224	
   225	      - name: Package
   226	        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
   227	        run: |
   228	          ./src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/appimage.sh build/package "$VERSION" \
   229	            "dist/JusPrin_Linux_AppImage_Ubuntu2404_V${VERSION}${{ inputs.arch && format('_{0}', inputs.arch) || '' }}.AppImage"
   230	
   231	      # What lets Sentry name the functions in a crash or a report's stack: each
   232	      # executable and library the app ships, with its PDB on Windows, filed by
   233	      # its build id, and the debug information split off above. The build
   234	      # fails unless Sentry then holds the app's own code's debug information,
   235	      # with file and line (Packaging/sentry_debug_files.sh). Sentry's address and
   236	      # the token that may upload stay in the repository's secrets.
   237	      - name: Upload debug files to Sentry
   238	        shell: bash
   239	        env:
   240	          SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN }}
   241	          SENTRY_URL: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_URL }}
   242	          SENTRY_ORG: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_ORG }}
   243	          SENTRY_PROJECT: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_PROJECT }}
   244	        run: |
   245	          case "$RUNNER_OS" in
   246	            Windows) main=build/src/Release/OrcaSlicer.dll; paths=(build/OrcaSlicer build/src/Release) ;;
   247	            macOS)
   248	              app="build/${{ inputs.arch }}/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer.app"
   249	              main="$app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer"; paths=("$app/Contents" "build/${{ inputs.arch }}/OrcaSlicer.dSYM") ;;
   250	            *) main=build/package/bin/orca-slicer; paths=(build/package/bin build/package/lib build/orca-slicer.debug) ;;
   251	          esac
   252	          ./src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/sentry_debug_files.sh upload "$main" "${paths[@]}"
   253	
   254	      # What lets Sentry name the Agent and Home pages' code in a page error's
   255	      # stack: each page and its source map, filed under this commit. Every
   256	      # platform builds the same pages; the step fails if one differs.
   257	      - name: Upload page source maps to Sentry
   258	        shell: bash
   259	        env:
   260	          SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN }}
   261	          SENTRY_URL: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_URL }}
   262	          SENTRY_ORG: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_ORG }}
   263	          SENTRY_PROJECT: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_PROJECT }}
   264	        run: ./src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/sentry_page_maps.sh upload
   265	
   266	      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
   267	        with:
   268	          name: jusprin-${{ runner.os }}-${{ inputs.arch || 'x64' }}
   269	          path: dist/*
   270	          if-no-files-found: error
   271	          # The release keeps the files; these only carry them to it.
   272	          retention-days: 7

   208	          # below, not shipped.
   209	          ./build_linux.sh -srlL -- -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS=-gline-tables-only -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS=-gline-tables-only

   213	      # split file keeps; without one the two would not match.

   223	          objcopy --strip-debug --add-gnu-debuglink=build/orca-slicer.debug "$bin"

   225	      - name: Package
   226	        if: runner.os == 'Linux'

   228	          ./src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/appimage.sh build/package "$VERSION" \
   229	            "dist/JusPrin_Linux_AppImage_Ubuntu2404_V${VERSION}${{ inputs.arch && format('_{0}', inputs.arch) || '' }}.AppImage"

   231	      # What lets Sentry name the functions in a crash or a report's stack: each

   233	      # its build id, and the debug information split off above. The build
   234	      # fails unless Sentry then holds the app's own code's debug information,

   236	      # the token that may upload stay in the repository's secrets.

   238	        shell: bash
   239	        env:
   240	          SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN }}
   241	          SENTRY_URL: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_URL }}
   242	          SENTRY_ORG: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_ORG }}
   243	          SENTRY_PROJECT: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_PROJECT }}

   245	          case "$RUNNER_OS" in
   246	            Windows) main=build/src/Release/OrcaSlicer.dll; paths=(build/OrcaSlicer build/src/Release) ;;
   247	            macOS)
   248	              app="build/${{ inputs.arch }}/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer.app"
   249	              main="$app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer"; paths=("$app/Contents" "build/${{ inputs.arch }}/OrcaSlicer.dSYM") ;;

   252	          ./src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/sentry_debug_files.sh upload "$main" "${paths[@]}"

   254	      # What lets Sentry name the Agent and Home pages' code in a page error's
   255	      # stack: each page and its source map, filed under this commit. Every
   256	      # platform builds the same pages; the step fails if one differs.
   257	      - name: Upload page source maps to Sentry
   258	        shell: bash
   259	        env:
   260	          SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN }}
   261	          SENTRY_URL: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_URL }}
   262	          SENTRY_ORG: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_ORG }}
   263	          SENTRY_PROJECT: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_PROJECT }}
   264	        run: ./src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/sentry_page_maps.sh upload
   265	
   266	      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
   267	        with:
   268	          name: jusprin-${{ runner.os }}-${{ inputs.arch || 'x64' }}
   269	          path: dist/*
   270	          if-no-files-found: error
   271	          # The release keeps the files; these only carry them to it.
   272	          retention-days: 7

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Gives Sentry what it needs to name the functions in a JusPrin crash or error
# report, with their file and line: the debug files of one platform's build
# (jusprin_release_build.yml), filed under their build ids.
#
#   sentry_debug_files.sh upload <main file> <folder or file>...
#       Uploads every debug file under the folders, then verifies <main file>.
#   sentry_debug_files.sh verify <main file>
#       Fails unless Sentry holds debug information (the "debug" feature:
#       functions with their file and line) for <main file>'s build id, each
#       architecture's in a universal Mac file. A symbol table alone names
#       functions only, so it does not count. The release skill runs it on a
#       released copy of the app.
#
# <main file> is the file that holds the app's own code: OrcaSlicer.dll on
# Windows (its PDB has the same build id), the app's executable on macOS (its
# dSYM) and Linux (its split .debug file). Reads SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN, SENTRY_URL, SENTRY_ORG and SENTRY_PROJECT,
# and fails without any of them.
set -euo pipefail

# The last 2.x: 3.x supports only self-hosted Sentry 24.11.1 and later.
cli=(npx --yes @sentry/cli@2.58.6)

missing=()
for name in SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN SENTRY_URL SENTRY_ORG SENTRY_PROJECT; do
    [ -n "${!name:-}" ] || missing+=("$name")
done
if [ ${#missing[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
    echo "::error::Sentry cannot get this build's debug files without the secret(s) ${missing[*]}; crash and error reports from it would show addresses only."
    exit 1
fi

command=${1:-}
main=${2:-}
if [ "$command" != upload ] && [ "$command" != verify ] || [ -z "$main" ]; then
    echo "usage: $0 upload <main file> <folder or file>... | verify <main file>" >&2
    exit 2
fi
shift 2
if [ ! -f "$main" ]; then
    echo "::error::$main does not exist."
    exit 1
fi

debug_ids=$("${cli[@]}" debug-files check --json "$main" |
    node -e 'let s="";process.stdin.on("data",d=>s+=d).on("end",()=>{const v=JSON.parse(s).variants||[];if(!v.length)process.exit(1);for(const x of v)console.log(x.debug_id)})')

if [ "$command" = upload ]; then
    if [ $# -eq 0 ]; then
        echo "usage: $0 upload <main file> <folder or file>..." >&2
        exit 2
    fi
    "${cli[@]}" debug-files upload --wait-for 600 "$@"
fi

# What Sentry holds under each build id, and whether any of it has file and line.
for debug_id in $debug_ids; do
    held=$(curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN" \
        "${SENTRY_URL%/}/api/0/projects/$SENTRY_ORG/$SENTRY_PROJECT/files/dsyms/?query=$debug_id")
    named=$(printf '%s' "$held" |
        node -e 'let s="";process.stdin.on("data",d=>s+=d).on("end",()=>{console.log(JSON.parse(s).filter(f=>(f.data?.features||[]).includes("debug")).length)})')
    if [ "$named" = 0 ]; then
        echo "::error::Sentry holds no debug information for $main (build id $debug_id), so its crash and error reports would show no file or line."
        exit 1
    fi
    echo "Sentry holds debug information for $main (build id $debug_id)."
done

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Gives Sentry what it needs to name the Agent and Home pages' own code in a
# page error's stack: each page's index.html and its source map
# (WebShared/inlinedScriptSourceMap.ts), filed under the app's release and the
# page's build (WebShared/errorReports.ts), at the names the page's frames
# carry: app:///agent/index.html and app:///home/index.html.
#
#   sentry_page_maps.sh upload
#       Run after a build, from the repository's top folder. Files this
#       build's pages and maps under JUSPRIN_PAGE_BUILD, the build the pages
#       were built with, then verifies them. A file Sentry already holds for
#       that build must be the same file; another platform's build of the same
#       commit uploads the same pages.
#   sentry_page_maps.sh verify [<resources folder>]
#       Fails unless Sentry holds, for this version, exactly these index.html
#       files (by content) and a source map beside each. <resources folder> is
#       the one that holds jusprin/agent and jusprin/home, by default the
#       repository's; the release skill passes a released app's.
#
# Reads SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN, SENTRY_URL, SENTRY_ORG and SENTRY_PROJECT, and
# fails without any of them. Sentry 23.1.1 finds a page's map by its frames'
# file name, release and dist only; it has no debug ids for JavaScript.
set -euo pipefail

top=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../../../../.." && pwd)

missing=()
for name in SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN SENTRY_URL SENTRY_ORG SENTRY_PROJECT; do
    [ -n "${!name:-}" ] || missing+=("$name")
done
if [ ${#missing[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
    echo "::error::Sentry cannot get the pages' source maps without the secret(s) ${missing[*]}; page error reports from this build would not name the pages' code."
    exit 1
fi

command=${1:-}
if [ "$command" != upload ] && [ "$command" != verify ]; then
    echo "usage: $0 upload | verify [<resources folder>]" >&2
    exit 2
fi
resources=${2:-$top/resources}

# The release the app's events carry (Updates/Version.hpp version_label()).
version=$(sed -n 's/.*kVersion\[\] = "\(.*\)";.*/\1/p' "$top/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp")
orca=$(sed -n 's/^set(SoftFever_VERSION "\(.*\)")/\1/p' "$top/version.inc")
release="JusPrin $version (OrcaSlicer $orca)"
encoded=$(node -e 'console.log(encodeURIComponent(process.argv[1]))' "$release")
api="${SENTRY_URL%/}/api/0"
files_api="$api/projects/$SENTRY_ORG/$SENTRY_PROJECT/releases/$encoded/files/"
auth=(-H "Authorization: Bearer $SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN")

page_html() { printf '%s/jusprin/%s/index.html' "$resources" "$1"; }
page_map() {
    case "$1" in
        agent) printf '%s/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/dist/index.html.map' "$top" ;;
        home) printf '%s/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/HomeUI/dist/index.html.map' "$top" ;;
    esac
}
sha1_of() { node -e 'console.log(require("crypto").createHash("sha1").update(require("fs").readFileSync(process.argv[1])).digest("hex"))' "$1"; }

# Every file Sentry holds for the release, one "<name>\t<dist>\t<sha1>\t<Sourcemap header>" per line.
held_files() {
    local cursor="" page
    while :; do
        page=$(curl -fsS -D "$headers_file" "${auth[@]}" "$files_api?per_page=100${cursor:+&cursor=$cursor}") || return 1
        printf '%s' "$page" | node -e 'let s="";process.stdin.on("data",d=>s+=d).on("end",()=>{for(const f of JSON.parse(s))console.log([f.name,f.dist??"",f.sha1,(f.headers||{}).Sourcemap??""].join("\t"))})'
        cursor=$(grep -i '^link:' "$headers_file" | sed -n 's/.*rel="next"; results="true"; cursor="\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')
        [ -n "$cursor" ] || return 0
    done
}
headers_file=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$headers_file"' EXIT

if [ "$command" = upload ]; then
    build=${JUSPRIN_PAGE_BUILD:-}
    if [ -z "$build" ]; then
        echo "::error::JUSPRIN_PAGE_BUILD names no build, so the pages carry none and Sentry could not tell their maps from another build's."

1:# JusPrin guide
13:## Before a release
15:The guide is brought in line with the app before each release, on a computer with the app built.
17:1. Build the app's test harness and pages from the commit to release: the `shell_integration_harness` and `jusprin_web` targets.
18:2. Leave the computer alone and run `scripts/check_guide.py --ask-ai`. It takes about a minute a page, plus the questions.
20:   - **A label is on no screen.** The app's wording changed. Find the new wording in the app and correct the page.
21:   - **A run failed.** Open its log, which the command names. Either the screen no longer works as the page says, and the page needs correcting, or the harness expects something the app no longer does, and the harness needs correcting.
22:   - **A picture is blank.** The program that started the command may not record the screen. Grant it Screen Recording in the system's privacy settings and run again.
24:4. Look through what changed on screen since the last release (`git log <last release tag>..HEAD -- src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin`). The command finds what a page gets wrong. It cannot find a new screen or menu item that no page mentions, so add those by hand.
25:5. Commit the pages together with their pictures, the skills the command rebuilt, and `checked-version.txt`. When every step passes for every page, the command writes the app's version to that file. A run with `--skip-app`, with `--area`, or without `--ask-ai` leaves it as it was. The release workflow refuses a version this file does not name. The file says the check passed for that version, not on which commit, so run it on the commit you mean to release.
27:## What the command does
29:1. **Walks the app and takes the pictures.** `tests/shell/guide_checks.json` names, for each page, the runs of the app's test harness that go through the screens the page describes, and the checks in each run the page depends on. `tests/shell/run_guide_checks.py` runs them in the app as built and copies the pictures a page uses into `pictures/<page>/`.
30:2. **Rebuilds the copy AI reads.** `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/guide.ts` builds a skill from each page.
32:4. **Asks AI the page's questions** (`--ask-ai`). `tests/project_prompt/guide_questions.json` holds them with what a right answer says. `tests/project_prompt/run_guide_tests.py` asks the model and has a judge read the replies.
34:## Writing a page
36:- Start it with `<!-- ai-description: … -->`: one line, at most 300 bytes, saying when AI should read it. The model reads every page's description together in one list, and the Claude command-line tool that `--ask-ai` runs through cuts a tool description longer than about 2,000 characters, so keep each one short: about 200 bytes. Write `...` rather than `…` in it, since that tool rewrites the one as the other.
38:- Use bold only for words that are on screen, exactly as they are on screen.
40:- A picture is kept at twice the screen's size, and the guide window shows it at half, the size it has on screen. Mark a run's picture that the harness draws at the screen's own size with `"atScreenSize": true`, and the command doubles it.

## Before a release

The guide is brought in line with the app before each release, on a computer with the app built.

1. Build the app's test harness and pages from the commit to release: the `shell_integration_harness` and `jusprin_web` targets.
2. Leave the computer alone and run `scripts/check_guide.py --ask-ai`. It takes about a minute a page, plus the questions.
3. Fix what it reports, then run it again until it passes:
   - **A label is on no screen.** The app's wording changed. Find the new wording in the app and correct the page.
   - **A run failed.** Open its log, which the command names. Either the screen no longer works as the page says, and the page needs correcting, or the harness expects something the app no longer does, and the harness needs correcting.
   - **A picture is blank.** The program that started the command may not record the screen. Grant it Screen Recording in the system's privacy settings and run again.
   - **AI answered a question wrongly.** Read its reply in the output. Usually the page is unclear or its first line does not say when to read it.
4. Look through what changed on screen since the last release (`git log <last release tag>..HEAD -- src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin`). The command finds what a page gets wrong. It cannot find a new screen or menu item that no page mentions, so add those by hand.
5. Commit the pages together with their pictures, the skills the command rebuilt, and `checked-version.txt`. When every step passes for every page, the command writes the app's version to that file. A run with `--skip-app`, with `--area`, or without `--ask-ai` leaves it as it was. The release workflow refuses a version this file does not name. The file says the check passed for that version, not on which commit, so run it on the commit you mean to release.

"""Checks the app guide (docs/guide) from end to end, and rebuilds what is
built from it. Run it after editing a page, and before a release.

  1. Walks each page's screens in the app as built and takes its pictures
     (tests/shell/run_guide_checks.py). Needs the shell_integration_harness
     and jusprin_web targets built from this checkout, and this computer's
     screen.
  2. Rebuilds the skill AI reads from each page, and checks that every label
     a page quotes is in the source, that every section has a run in step 1,
     that every picture is one step 1 took, and that every page has questions
     for step 3 (AgentUI's guide.test.ts).
  3. With --ask-ai: asks the model each page's questions and has a judge read
     the answers (tests/project_prompt/run_guide_tests.py), on the Claude
     subscription unless told otherwise after `--`.

    scripts/check_guide.py
    scripts/check_guide.py --area print-settings --ask-ai
    scripts/check_guide.py --skip-app             steps 2 and 3 only
    scripts/check_guide.py --ask-ai -- --runs 1   options after -- go to step 3

every page passes, it writes the app's version (Updates/Version.hpp) to
docs/guide/checked-version.txt. Commit that file with the pages: the release
workflow refuses a version the guide was not checked for. The file says the

# Project chat prompt tests

The project chat's assistant is a system prompt
(`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/projectInstructions.ts`), the project
tools and the chat. `run_prompt_tests.py` asks the live model for its next
step at a known point of a project chat and checks that step against one
sentence of the prompt. After an edit it runs once, on the checkout, and
prints each case beside a baseline kept in the repository (`baseline.json`;
see "Judging a prompt or skill change"). The app does not run.

On Kenneth's local machine, the keys are in
`~/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env` (outside the repository, mode `600`). An
agent running this suite can load them for that command in a subshell:

```bash
( . "$HOME/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env"; tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py )
```

Do not print, copy into the repository, or include the key values in a command
or test log. The file exports `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_API_KEY`; the
runner reads them from its environment. No run happens without Kenneth
approving that batch (case count, runs, token estimate). A `403 Key limit
exceeded` means stop; do not switch keys.

The model, hosts and judge are the printer suite's (`tests/printer_prompt`,
"Which model"): DeepSeek V4 Flash through OpenRouter, pinned to Alibaba,
Novita, Baidu and AtlasCloud, with a pinned OpenAI judge. `--backend
claude-cli` runs the same cases on the developer's Claude subscription
instead, for iterating on a prompt without API cost (see "Running on the
Claude subscription").

## One step, with its reads answered

Each case starts at a point recorded from the app and judges the model's next
step: a reply, or its tool calls. One response may hold several calls. The
### Which backend for what

- **Iterating on a prompt or skill: the subscription.** A strong model
  answering the app's real requests, with real tool calls, shows what the
  prompt itself causes: an ambiguous sentence, a rule two sections disagree
  on, a skill that invites the wrong call. It costs no API money, so it can
  be run as often as the subscription's usage limits allow. Those limits are
  shared with the developer's own Claude Code work; start with one case and
  keep `--jobs` small.
- **Before a release: a small paid run on the app's default model.** The app
  defaults to `gpt-5.4-mini` (the OpenAI provider's default in
  `ProviderProfile.hpp`), which scored about like DeepSeek V4 Flash in the
  printer suite's model table (82 and 79 of 87, `tests/printer_prompt`,
  "Which model"). A strong model
  can paper over an ambiguity a weaker one trips on, so a pass on Opus does
  not show the shipped default will pass. That run needs Kenneth's approval
  like every paid batch.
- **The baselines** are DeepSeek V4 Flash with the OpenAI judge
  (`baseline.json`), except the subscription baseline, which is claude-cli's
  own (`baseline-claude-cli.json`, which `--backend claude-cli` compares with).
  A claude-cli count is compared only with that one. Changing the judge
README.md

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Collect JusPrin's own interface text into its translation catalogs.

JusPrin keeps its translations apart from OrcaSlicer's, so taking a new
OrcaSlicer release never conflicts in a catalog:

  * native/JusPrin.pot and native/<lang>.po hold the text the native windows
    mark with _L, _u8L, L, _L_CONTEXT and _L_PLURAL under src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin.
    Text OrcaSlicer's own template already has is left out: its translations
    come from upstream. Brand/brand_catalogs.py merges these into the catalog
    the app loads.
  * pages/<lang>.po hold the text of the AI and Home pages, marked with the
    Lingui macros (t, Trans, Plural). Lingui's own extractor writes them.

Run it after marking or changing text, then translate the new entries:

    python3 src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/update_catalogs.py

Needs GNU gettext (xgettext, msgmerge, msgcat, msgcomm) and the pages'
node_modules (npm ci in AgentUI).
"""

import json
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
JUSPRIN = HERE.parent
ROOT = JUSPRIN.parents[3]
UPSTREAM_I18N = ROOT / "localization" / "i18n"
NATIVE = HERE / "native"
PAGES = HERE / "pages"

# The keywords upstream's scripts/run_gettext.sh passes, and
# translated_plural from Support/Translate.hpp.
XGETTEXT_KEYWORDS = [
19:Needs GNU gettext (xgettext, msgmerge, msgcat, msgcomm) and the pages'
20:node_modules (npm ci in AgentUI).
46:SKIP_DIRS = {"Testing", "AgentUI", "HomeUI", "WebShared", "node_modules", "Localization"}
89:        run("xgettext", *XGETTEXT_KEYWORDS, "--add-comments=TRN", "--from-code=UTF-8", "--no-location",
108:            # upstream's plural rule; msgmerge then adds every entry with as
116:        run("msgmerge", "--quiet", "-N", "--no-wrap", "--previous", "-U", "--backup=none", str(po), str(pot))
122:    npx = shutil.which("npx") or shutil.which("npx.cmd")
123:    if npx is None:
124:        sys.exit("update_catalogs: npx not found; the page catalogs need Node")
125:    run(npx, "lingui", "extract", "--clean", cwd=JUSPRIN / "AgentUI")

commit 7dee738e404736d6a508759f34f5a8a7fade49a0
Author: Kenneth Jiang <kenneth.jiang@gmail.com>
Date:   Tue Nov 17 16:20:54 2026 -0800

    jusprin-release skill: fix what a cold read found it would miss or get wrong
    
    A read-only review checked the skill against the workflows, scripts and
    docs it relies on. Changes:
    
    - The range is fixed at a recorded commit. Before landing, the skill checks
      whether jusprin-dev moved; commits that landed meanwhile get the checks
      before they can reach main, and main is moved to the exact release commit.
    - The release workflow neither builds nor runs the tests on any platform
      (build_win.bat -s -i, build_linux.sh -srlL, build_release_macos.sh pass no
      test flag). The skill said it compiled them on Windows and Linux.
    - Server addresses: many are joined from pieces (/o/token/, /o/revoke_token/,
      /accounts/..., /jusprin/api/me/, /models, /ent/jusprin/v2/auth/<step>), so
      the single grep missed them. The skill now lists them from the code that
      builds them and checks full paths only.
    - Translations point to Localization/README.md and JusPrin's own catalogs,
      not upstream's localization/i18n and run_gettext.
    - Error-handling findings: Kenneth says which must be fixed; a fix's push
      needs his yes; the tsd-enterprise range is defined by date.
    - Tests: the configure line for a fresh worktree, the tool_call_check
      target, Windows and Linux test flags, and the paid default-model prompt
      run the prompt README asks for before a release.
    - Guide: new screens are added before the check runs, not after it passed.
    - Sentry: gh secret list answers 403 for this computer's token, so the skill
      no longer runs it; Kenneth supplies the read-only values for verifying the
      draft, which are never written to a file.
    - The release publisher is JUSPRIN_RELEASE_PUBLISHER or kennethjiang; the
      run id comes from gh run list; the release environment may hold the draft
      job for approval.
    - Before publishing, winget_updater.yml (inherited from OrcaSlicer, submits
      as SoftFever.OrcaSlicer on publish) must still be disabled.
    
    Entire-Checkpoint: 01M7P0EA1KJ11Z4ZP47HM8PGV8

# JusPrin error handling: audit

The rules are the Error handling section of `AGENTS.md` (JusPrin, the desktop
app) and of `CLAUDE.md` (tsd-enterprise, the JusPrin Cloud server). Read that
section first; this skill only says how to check code against it. Checking
production for failures over a period is the `jusprin-production-check` skill
in the tsd-enterprise repository.

The server's expected-errors table is `EXPECTED` in
`web_ent/jusprin/v2/errors.py`; the app has no table yet. The app reports
through `report_unexpected_error`, the server through Sentry. List an outcome
that looks designed but has no table entry apart from the other findings.

## Audit a commit range

Input: a repository and a range, such as `jusprin/v2.0.0..jusprin-dev`.

The audit is one question, asked of every place the changed code decides what
happened: **can the person do something about it, and did Kenneth decide what
they are told?** Do not search for particular
code shapes. Each failure this audit exists for had a shape nobody had listed,
and a list only finds what its writer already thought of.

1. List the changed code: `git diff --stat <range>`, then read each changed
   function whole in JusPrin's own code (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`, the
   pages, `web_ent/jusprin/`). Read the function, not the diff lines: what a
   change leaves the rest of the function to assume is where failures hide.
2. Wherever the code decides what happened (an outcome, a state, a record,
   what the person is told, whether work goes on), ask the question.
   - Yes to both: there is an entry in the expected-errors table for that
     named cause. Go to step 4.
   - Otherwise the code is dealing with an unexpected error. Go to step 3.
     A sentence, a code or a branch of its own for a failure the person can
     do nothing about (a provider or our server slow, overloaded, down or
     limiting us) is a finding, even when it looks carefully designed.
3. For an unexpected error the rules allow almost no code, so the code is
   the finding. Two things only are allowed:
   - turning a failure that arrived as a value into a thrown error on the
     spot, keeping the other side's status, request id and error text and
     the request's own facts (user, chat, turn, model), with no
     interpretation;
   - the one handler at the top of an entry point, which reports through the
     reporting function and tells the person "Something went wrong on our
     side", with nothing more specific.
   Everything else is a finding: work that goes on after a failure nobody
   decided on, a value or a sentence invented for it, a retry, a report call
   anywhere but the top handler, a failure recorded as a success, and the
   other side's status, request id or error text dropped on the way up. Also
   follow one failure up from each entry point the change touches and say
   whether it reaches a handler that reports it and tells the person.
4. Read every new or changed entry in the expected-errors tables, and every
   place that catches. Flag an entry whose cause is a status code, an
   exception type or "the request was not valid", an entry the person can do

call :add_arg build_deps bool d deps "Download and build the dependencies, needed before -s"

call :add_arg pack_deps bool p pack "Bundle the built dependencies into a zip file"

call :add_arg use_msvc bool "" msvc "Use cl as the compiler (default)"
call :add_arg use_ninja bool x ninja "Use the Ninja Multi-Config generator"
call :add_arg use_msbuild bool "" msbuild "Use the Visual Studio generator (default)"
call :add_arg vs_version string "" vs "Visual Studio release: 2019, 2022 or 2026 (default: autodetect)"
call :add_arg clang_path string "" clang-path "Path to clang-cl.exe, requires -x (default: the one from Visual Studio)"
call :add_arg cache string "" cache "Compiler cache: ccache, sccache or off, requires -l -x (default: off)"

call :add_section "How much gets rebuilt"
call :add_arg slicer_target string "" slicer-target "Build one slicer target instead of all, e.g. libslic3r"
call :add_arg deps_target string t deps-target "Build one dependency instead of all, e.g. dep_Boost"
call :add_arg no_configure bool "" no-configure "Build the existing tree without configuring"
)

call :resolve_clang_cl
%repeat_error%

if "%using_ninja%" == "ON" (
	if "%use_clang_cl%" == "ON" (
		REM Quoted, because the resolved path has spaces in it.
		set "gen_args=-DCMAKE_C_COMPILER="!clang_exe!" -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER="!clang_exe!""
	)
) else (
	set "gen_args=-A !arch!"
	if "%use_clang_cl%" == "ON" (
		set "gen_args=!gen_args! -T ClangCL"
	)
)

if not "%clang_path%" == "" if not "%using_ninja%" == "ON" (
    echo --clang-path needs the Ninja generator; add -x. The Visual Studio
    echo generator builds clang-cl through its own ClangCL toolset.
    exit /b 1
    echo "   -e: build in RelWithDebInfo mode"
    echo "   -F: rebuild the cached Docker/Podman runner image from scratch when used with -g"
    echo "   -g: run the requested build steps inside a Docker/Podman Ubuntu 24.04 container similar to the GitHub Actions Linux runner"
    echo "   -h: prints this help text"
    echo "   -i: build the Orca Slicer AppImage (optional)"
    echo "   -p: disable precompiled headers (on by default): more ccache hits after header changes, slower misses"
    echo "   -r: skip RAM and disk checks (low RAM compiling)"
    echo "   -s: build the Orca Slicer (optional)"
    echo "   -t: build tests (optional), requires -s flag"
    echo "   -u: install system dependencies (asks for sudo password; build prerequisite)"
    echo "   -l: use Clang instead of GCC (default: GCC)"
    echo "   -L: use ld.lld as linker (if available)"
    echo "   -- CMAKE_ARGS...: pass everything after '--' to the cmake configure step of the deps (-d) and OrcaSlicer (-s/-t) builds,"
    echo "       e.g. -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS=\"-O2 -march=native\", -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=g++-14, -DCMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS=-fuse-ld=mold."
    echo "       They come last on the cmake command line, so they override what -l and -L set."
    echo "For a first use, you want to './${SCRIPT_NAME} -u'"
        if [[ -n "${SAVED_PARALLEL_LEVEL}" ]] ; then
            export CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL=${SAVED_PARALLEL_LEVEL}
        else
            unset CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL
        fi
    fi
fi

if [[ -n "${BUILD_ORCA}" ]] || [[ -n "${BUILD_TESTS}" ]] ; then
    echo "Configuring OrcaSlicer..."
    if [[ -n "${CLEAN_BUILD}" ]] ; then
        print_and_run rm -fr $BUILD_DIR
    fi
    read -r -a BUILD_ARGS <<< "${ORCA_EXTRA_BUILD_ARGS}"
    if [[ $BUILD_CONFIG != Release ]] ; then
        BUILD_ARGS+=(-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE="${BUILD_CONFIG}")
    fi
    if [[ -n "${BUILD_TESTS}" ]] ; then
        BUILD_ARGS+=(-DBUILD_TESTS=ON)
    fi
    if [[ -n "${ORCA_UPDATER_SIG_KEY}" ]] ; then
        BUILD_ARGS+=(-DORCA_UPDATER_SIG_KEY="${ORCA_UPDATER_SIG_KEY}")
    fi

    print_and_run cmake -S . -B $BUILD_DIR "${CMAKE_C_CXX_COMPILER_CLANG[@]}" "${CMAKE_LLD_LINKER_ARGS[@]}" "${CMAKE_CCACHE_ARGS[@]}" -G "Ninja Multi-Config" \
-DSLIC3R_PCH=${SLIC3R_PRECOMPILED_HEADERS} \
-DORCA_TOOLS=ON \
"${COLORED_OUTPUT}" \
"${BUILD_ARGS[@]}" \
"${EXTRA_CMAKE_ARGS[@]}"
    echo "done"
    if [[ -n "${BUILD_ORCA}" ]]; then
	echo "Building OrcaSlicer ..."
	print_and_run cmake --build $BUILD_DIR --config "${BUILD_CONFIG}" --target OrcaSlicer
	echo "Building OrcaSlicer_profile_validator .."
	print_and_run cmake --build $BUILD_DIR --config "${BUILD_CONFIG}" --target OrcaSlicer_profile_validator
	echo "Building generate_system_cache ..."
	print_and_run cmake --build $BUILD_DIR --config "${BUILD_CONFIG}" --target generate_system_cache
	./scripts/run_gettext.sh
    fi
    if [[ -n "${BUILD_TESTS}" ]] ; then
	echo "Building tests ..."
	print_and_run cmake --build ${BUILD_DIR} --config "${BUILD_CONFIG}" --target tests/all
    fi
    echo "done"
fi

if [[ -n "${BUILD_IMAGE}" || -n "${BUILD_ORCA}" ]] ; then
    pushd $BUILD_DIR > /dev/null
    build_linux_image="./src/build_linux_image.sh"
    if [[ -e ${build_linux_image} ]] ; then
        extra_script_args=""
        if [[ -n "${BUILD_IMAGE}" ]] ; then
            extra_script_args="-i"
        fi
        print_and_run ${build_linux_image} ${extra_script_args} -R "${BUILD_CONFIG}"

        echo "done"
    fi
    popd > /dev/null # build
fi

    echo "   -i: build the Orca Slicer AppImage (optional)"
    echo "   -p: disable precompiled headers (on by default): more ccache hits after header changes, slower misses"
    echo "   -r: skip RAM and disk checks (low RAM compiling)"
    echo "   -s: build the Orca Slicer (optional)"
    echo "   -t: build tests (optional), requires -s flag"
    echo "   -u: install system dependencies (asks for sudo password; build prerequisite)"
    echo "   -l: use Clang instead of GCC (default: GCC)"
    echo "   -L: use ld.lld as linker (if available)"
    echo "   -- CMAKE_ARGS...: pass everything after '--' to the cmake configure step of the deps (-d) and OrcaSlicer (-s/-t) builds,"
    echo "       e.g. -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS=\"-O2 -march=native\", -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=g++-14, -DCMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS=-fuse-ld=mold."
    echo "       They come last on the cmake command line, so they override what -l and -L set."
    echo "For a first use, you want to './${SCRIPT_NAME} -u'"
        if [[ -n "${SAVED_PARALLEL_LEVEL}" ]] ; then
            export CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL=${SAVED_PARALLEL_LEVEL}
        else
            unset CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL
        fi
    fi
fi

if [[ -n "${BUILD_ORCA}" ]] || [[ -n "${BUILD_TESTS}" ]] ; then
    echo "Configuring OrcaSlicer..."
    if [[ -n "${CLEAN_BUILD}" ]] ; then
        print_and_run rm -fr $BUILD_DIR
    fi
    read -r -a BUILD_ARGS <<< "${ORCA_EXTRA_BUILD_ARGS}"
    if [[ $BUILD_CONFIG != Release ]] ; then
        BUILD_ARGS+=(-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE="${BUILD_CONFIG}")
    fi
    if [[ -n "${BUILD_TESTS}" ]] ; then
        BUILD_ARGS+=(-DBUILD_TESTS=ON)
    fi
    if [[ -n "${ORCA_UPDATER_SIG_KEY}" ]] ; then
        BUILD_ARGS+=(-DORCA_UPDATER_SIG_KEY="${ORCA_UPDATER_SIG_KEY}")
    fi

    print_and_run cmake -S . -B $BUILD_DIR "${CMAKE_C_CXX_COMPILER_CLANG[@]}" "${CMAKE_LLD_LINKER_ARGS[@]}" "${CMAKE_CCACHE_ARGS[@]}" -G "Ninja Multi-Config" \
-DSLIC3R_PCH=${SLIC3R_PRECOMPILED_HEADERS} \
-DORCA_TOOLS=ON \
"${COLORED_OUTPUT}" \
"${BUILD_ARGS[@]}" \
"${EXTRA_CMAKE_ARGS[@]}"
    echo "done"
    if [[ -n "${BUILD_ORCA}" ]]; then
	echo "Building OrcaSlicer ..."
	print_and_run cmake --build $BUILD_DIR --config "${BUILD_CONFIG}" --target OrcaSlicer
	echo "Building OrcaSlicer_profile_validator .."
	print_and_run cmake --build $BUILD_DIR --config "${BUILD_CONFIG}" --target OrcaSlicer_profile_validator
	echo "Building generate_system_cache ..."
	print_and_run cmake --build $BUILD_DIR --config "${BUILD_CONFIG}" --target generate_system_cache
	./scripts/run_gettext.sh
    fi
    if [[ -n "${BUILD_TESTS}" ]] ; then
	echo "Building tests ..."
	print_and_run cmake --build ${BUILD_DIR} --config "${BUILD_CONFIG}" --target tests/all
    fi
    echo "done"
fi

if [[ -n "${BUILD_IMAGE}" || -n "${BUILD_ORCA}" ]] ; then
    pushd $BUILD_DIR > /dev/null
    build_linux_image="./src/build_linux_image.sh"
    if [[ -e ${build_linux_image} ]] ; then
        extra_script_args=""
        if [[ -n "${BUILD_IMAGE}" ]] ; then
            extra_script_args="-i"
        fi
        print_and_run ${build_linux_image} ${extra_script_args} -R "${BUILD_CONFIG}"

        echo "done"
    fi
    popd > /dev/null # build
fi
